key_insight: A high-order multiscale method captures heterogeneous, fractionally damped wave propagation with an O(ε) global energy-norm error estimate.
engineering_relevance: The method reduces the computational burden of simulating history-dependent wave attenuation in composite materials compared with full-scale direct numerical simulation.
method: Derive a homogenized wave equation and first- and second-order corrections through multiscale asymptotic expansion.
Establish local residual cancellation, global error bounds, and unconditional shifted-energy stability.
Combine finite elements and finite differences using a fully discrete L2-1σ–Newmark scheme.
evidence_signal: Two- and three-dimensional numerical examples demonstrate accuracy, efficiency, reduced cost, and robustness, although the abstract reports no quantitative benchmarks.
watch_item: Fractional damping requires history-dependent calculations; the abstract does not specify long-time memory costs or history-compression strategies.
paper_title: A high-order multi-scale method and its error analysis for nonlocal-in-time fractionally damped wave problems in composite materials
